meta.title: Tesuch guide — why, what you gain and how to start
meta.description: A step-by-step guide to Tesuch for accounting firms and employers in Armenia: why to check labour-law deadlines before an inspection, what you gain, and how to set it up in ten steps.

hero.title: Find the gaps before the inspector does
hero.subtitle: Tesuch checks your employment contracts every night, scores your inspection readiness and warns you before a legal deadline is missed. This guide shows why it helps and how to start in ten steps.
hero.printHint: Send this guide to a client: in the print dialog choose “Save as PDF”.
hero.demoNote: All screenshots use fictional demo data. The interface is shown in Armenian.

nav.done: No time? We do it for you

why.title: Why check before an inspection
why.intro: In Armenia, employers are checked by the Health and Labour Inspection Body. It looks at whether employment contracts and HR practice follow the Labour Code. An inspection is the worst moment to learn that something was missed.
why.problemsNote: These are the typical areas that Tesuch checks. They are examples of where deadlines hide, not statistics.

problems.d: The probation end date is missing, unclear or has already passed without a decision.
The end date comes and goes, or the ground for a fixed term is not recorded.
A dismissal is prepared without the notice period being counted correctly.
Annual leave is not tracked, so entitlements and balances drift.
Employment contracts are not yet entered in the State Revenue Committee electronic system, and nobody sees which ones are missing.

why.cost: During an inspection you can only explain. A week earlier you can still fix the data, sign the right order and close the gap. What follows from a violation is set by law and by the inspector’s decision, so Tesuch quotes no fine amounts. The point is simple: it is cheaper to know today than to find out during the visit.

gain.title: What you gain
gain.firmIntro: You carry the HR paperwork of many clients. Tesuch gives you one place to see all of them.

firm.d: Every company in one list, the riskiest on top, so you know where to start this week.
The inspection-readiness score from 0 to 100 answers one question: would this company pass today?
Every night the rules go through every contract, so nobody has to remember the dates.
A new issue reaches you on Telegram and by email, and every Monday you get a weekly digest.
Draft orders and notices in Armenian, plus a checklist of all open issues in one PDF.
Owner, accountant and viewer: everyone sees and edits exactly what they should.
A record of who changed what and when, for your own peace of mind.

gain.ownerIntro: You do not read the Labour Code and you live in Telegram. Tesuch meets you there.

owner.d: One message on Monday: do I have a problem, and what are the one to three things to fix.
Each issue says what is wrong and what to do about it, with the Labour Code article and an arlis.am link where the article is verified.
Message the bot to get your score or the list of open problems whenever you want.
Ten questions, two minutes, no sign-up: a first picture before you decide anything.

how.title: How to use Tesuch, step by step
how.intro: Ten steps from the first sign-in to the weekly routine. The whole setup takes about as long as a coffee.

steps.t: Sign in with an email code
steps.d: Open Tesuch, press Sign in, enter your email and press “Send sign-in code”. Type the code from the email and press “Sign in”. No password is needed. If the code has expired, ask for a new one.
alts: The sign-in page: an email field and a field for the code from the email.

steps.d: On the first sign-in you see the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy. Read them and tick both boxes to continue. This happens once, and again only if the texts change.
alts: The consent page with the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy and two checkboxes.

steps.d: Type the name of your firm and press “Create”. The firm is your workspace. All your client companies live in it, and other firms never see your data. An employer can simply create a firm for their own company.
alts: The firm creation form with one name field.

steps.t: Add a company or import staff
steps.d: On the dashboard press “Add company”, or press “Load demo data” to try Tesuch on five fictional companies first. To load real staff, open Import, pick the company and upload a CSV or Excel file. Tesuch recognises headers in Armenian, Russian and English, and an ArmSoft export works too. Check the column mapping, look at the rows with errors in the preview and press “Import”.
alts: The import wizard: company selection, file upload and a button to download a CSV template.

steps.t: Read the score and the issues
steps.d: Each company has an inspection-readiness score from 0 to 100, and the riskiest are on top. Open a company to see its issues. Each one has a type: Violation (fix now), Attention (a deadline is close), Advisory (the rule is not yet verified by a lawyer) or Reminder. The deadline and the Labour Code article are shown next to it.
alts: The dashboard with fictional demo companies, each with a score, sorted from the riskiest.
A demo company page with its open issues, their types and deadlines.

steps.d: Press “Fix data”, correct the employee or contract data (for example the probation end or the ground for a fixed term) and save. At the next check the issue closes by itself, and “Re-check now” runs it at once. Use “Dismiss” only when you are sure the issue does not apply to you.
alts: The employee edit form with contract fields such as probation end and fixed-term ground.

steps.d: Open Settings, then Notifications, and press “Connect Telegram”. The Tesuch bot opens in Telegram: press Start. Press “Send test alert” to check that it works. From then on you get alerts on new issues and a digest every Monday, and you can write to the bot:
alts: The notifications settings with the Connect Telegram button and a test alert button.

steps.d: In Documents choose a company. You can download a checklist with all open issues in one PDF, and draft orders and notices for the end of probation, the end of a fixed-term contract and dismissal. All templates are drafts: show them to a lawyer before use.
alts: The documents page with a company and buttons to download the checklist and the drafts.

steps.d: Open Team and invite a colleague by email. Pick a role: an owner manages the firm, an accountant edits data, a viewer only looks. Every change is recorded in the audit log.
alts: The team page with the list of members, their roles and an invitation form.

steps.d: Every week the Quiz section offers five questions on the Labour Code. A week counts as clean if you took the quiz and there are no overdue violations at the end of it. A streak of clean weeks earns badges.
alts: The quiz page with a question and a panel of streaks and badges.

limits.title: Honest limits
limits.intro: Tesuch is an information tool. It is built to be careful about what it claims.

items.d: Tesuch does not replace a lawyer. Before you decide anything, talk to a lawyer and check the current text of the law on arlis.am.
The rules have not yet been reviewed by a lawyer. Until they are, every issue is marked “Advisory: not yet verified by a lawyer”, and an unverified rule never shows as a violation.
Orders and notices are drafts to be reviewed, not final legal documents.
No payroll, overtime or working-time checks yet, and no direct connection to the State Revenue Committee system: registration is a flag you set by hand.

items.a: No. Tesuch is an information tool. Rules marked “Advisory” are not yet verified by a lawyer. Consult a lawyer and check the current law on arlis.am before you decide.

items.q: What data do I have to upload?
items.a: A staff list with the contract dates: names, contract type, start and end, probation end and similar. Tesuch does not need salaries or passport data for its checks.

items.q: Do I need to be an accounting firm?
items.a: No. A firm is just a workspace. An employer can create one for their own company, or take the free self-check first without signing up.
The self-check is free and needs no account. The terms for firms are not published on this page, so ask us before you plan around a price.

items.q: Where is the data stored and who can see it?
items.a: In a data centre in the EU. Every firm sees only its own companies, and access inside a firm depends on the role of the person.

done.title: No time? We do it for you
done.intro: You do not have to set anything up yourself. Pick the way that suits you.

items.d: Export your staff list from ArmSoft, 1C or any other system as Excel or CSV and send it to us. The Tesuch team imports it. Technically, you invite the Tesuch team as “Accountant” in Team, and you can remove that access at any time.

items.t: Your accounting firm sets it up
items.d: If you work with an accounting firm, it can set everything up for you. You only read the Telegram digest.
Names or codes, date of birth and contract dates are enough. No salaries, passport data or addresses.
